sentences.text: Date of order 01-02-2025  JUDGMENT
The Police Sub-Inspector of Sanjay Nagara Police Station submitted charge sheet against accused for the offence punishable under Section 498(A), 323 of Indian Penal Code.
2. Prosecution Case:
The marriage of CW1 namely Smt. Sumithra and accused was solemnized on 23/04/2000.

After marriage, CW1 was residing with accused at Manjuantha Layout, Ngashettyhalli,
Bengaluru, at that time, the accused started to ill- treat CW1 and subjected her to mental and physical cruelty, unable to bear the torture, CW1 left KABC030690912021 CC No.25229/2021 matrimonial house and started resided at office No.36, NGEF Layout where she is working.

That being so, on 30-06-2021 at 6.30 p.m. when she was doing cleaning work in front of Bank of India, 5 th Main Road, NGEF Layout within the limits of Sanjay Nagara Police Station, accused came therein and abused her in filthiest language, beaten her with his hands and pushed her from the stairs and on account of which she succumbed to simple injury.
3. First Information Report:

On the basis of first information given by informant cum CW1 namely Smt. Sumithra, the HC of Sanjaynagara police station Sri Anjanmurthy registered Crime No.123/2021 against the accused for the offence punishable under Section 498(A) IPC, prepared FIR and sent the same to the Court and to his superior officers.
4. Investigation:

After registration of case, CW10 Sri Nagesh.H.V.,, PSI of Sanjay Nagara PS, drawn spot mahazar as per Ex.P2 on 01-07-2021, recorded the requisite witnesses and collected the documents and submitted the charge sheet against accused for the offence punishable under Sec.498A, 323 of IPC.
KABC030690912021 CC No.25229/2021 5. On receipt of charge sheet, this Court took cognizance of offence alleged against the accused.
6. The accused was enlarged on bail by the order dated 05/08/2022.
7. Copies of prosecution papers as required U/Sec.207 of Cr.P.C have been furnished to the accused.
8. Charge:

After hearing learned Sr.APP and counsel for accused, charge for the offences punishable U/Sec.498(A), 323 of Indian Penal Code, has been framed, read over and explained to the accused in the language known to him, who, in turn, pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
9. Prosecution Evidence:
The prosecution in order to establish its case cited 10 witnesses and examined 1 witness and exhibited 3 documents.

The learned Senior APP prayed for issuance of witness summons to other witnesses however his prayer was rejected on the ground that the PW1 being material witness did not support the case and hence the prosecution side was taken as closed Sumitra vs Rama Krishna D R on 1 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8104546/

sentences.text: KABC030690912021 CC No.25229/2021 10. Accused statement as per section 313 of CrPC: There are no incriminating evidences against the accused found from the evidence of prosecution thereby the recording of statement of accused as per Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. is dispensed with.
11. Heard the arguments.
Perused materials on the record.

12. The following point are arises for consideration is as follows;
1.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that after marriage of accused with CW1 Smt. Sumithra, accused started to ill-treat her and subjected her to both physically and mentally cruelty thereby resulted in commission of the offence punishable under Sec.498(A) of IPC?

2. Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on 30-06-2021 at 6.30 p.m. in front of Bank of India, 5th Main Road, NGEF KABC030690912021 CC No.25229/2021 Layout within the limits of Sanjay Nagara Police Station, accused beaten CW1 with his hands and pushed her from the stairs and caused simple injury thereby resulted in commission of the offence punishable under Sec.323 of IPC?
3. What order?
13.

The findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1& 2: In the Negative Point No.3 : As per final order REASONS 14. Point No.1: These points are taken up together for the purpose of common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts as they form the same part of transaction.

In support of prosecution case as narrated in paragraph 2 and the point for consideration in paragraph 12 of this judgment, the prosecution has examined one witness, which is as follows:
KABC030690912021 CC No.25229/2021 i. CW1 by name Smt. Sumithra, being Informant examined as PW1 identified her signatures on Ex.P1 and Ex.P2 (Spot Mahazar) as Ex.P1(a) and 2(a).

She further stated that when she went to police station for sorting out minor differences of opinion amongst her and accused, the police obtained her signatures on the said documents and she pleaded ignorance about the contents of Ex.P1 and 2.
In this regard, the learned Sr.APP cross examined this witness by treating her as hostile witness but no favorable answer has been elicited from her to support the prosecution case.

In her cross examination she deposed that:

Her denial of further statement given before police is marked as per Ex.P3.
15.
In this case, PW1 is the informant cum victim did not support the prosecution case.
Though the prosecution has cross examined her by treating as hostile witness, no favorable answers has been KABC030690912021 CC No.25229/2021 elicited from her to support the prosecution case.
However it appears from the cross examination of PW1 that the differences of opinion between the accused and her have been settled and they were living together.
Under this background, this court feels it is a waste of precious time of the Court in examining other witnesses.
Moreover the evidence of other witnesses is only formal in nature.

Therefore, the prayer of learned Sr.APP is rejected and prosecution evidence is taken as closed and hence the offence under section 498A of IPC with other offence under section 323 of IPC was not proved beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, this court answer the point No.1 and 2 in the Negative.

16. Point No.3:- In view of the above findings and reasons given on point No.1 and 2, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER Acting U/Sec.248(1) of the Cr.P.C.
(i) The accused is found not guilty and acquitted from the offence punishable under Sec.498(A), 323 of Indian Penal Code.
(ii) Accused is set at liberty.
KABC030690912021 CC No.25229/2021 (iii) In view of Section 437-A of Cr.P.C his bail bond shall be in force for 6 (six) months.
(iv) Ordered accordingly.
